description: Topic index for the ESSCE 2023 General Knowledge paper (gk-2023-matric, code 3133). No textbook – topics follow a general-knowledge hierarchy (tools/lib/gk_topics.py); refs are general sources.

topics.title: Eritrea – geography, history, society and institutions
topics.unit: General Knowledge (no textbook – verified against reliable general sources)
topics.concept: Know Eritrea's six zobas (Maekel, Debub, Anseba, Gash-Barka, Northern Red Sea, Southern Red Sea), its landforms and climate zones, main towns, historical sites, languages, national symbols and institutions.

subtopics.title: Physical geography, zobas and towns
subtopics.concept: Highlands (Maekel, Debub, parts of Anseba), western lowlands (Gash-Barka), eastern escarpment (Nefasit, Ghinda) and the coastal plain/Danakil depression (Southern Red Sea – the hottest and lowest part). Only Maekel borders no foreign country.

textbook_refs.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eritrea: land; Ras Doumeira
Eritrean MoE Geography Grade 9–12 (climate of Eritrea); FAO – Eritrea country profile

subtopics.title: Historical and archaeological sites
subtopics.concept: Ancient sites: Qohaito, Metera, Adulis, Keskese, Belew Kelew; Asmara's modernist architecture became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2017.

textbook_refs.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – 1st September: the beginning of the armed struggle
Eritrea National Museum / Commission of Culture and Sports; UNESCO – Asmara: A Modernist African City
Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – Italian colonization; ehrea.org – forgotten Eritrean heroes who resisted Italian rule
Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eritrea: history (Afabet 1988); Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com)
Abbate et al. (1998) Nature – A one-million-year-old Homo cranium from the Danakil (Afar) depression of Eritrea

subtopics.title: Languages, culture and national symbols
subtopics.concept: Nine ethnic languages; Tigrinya and Tigre use the Ge'ez (Ethiopic) script, Kunama and Bilen commonly use the Latin script, Arabic its own script. National emblem: the camel.

textbook_refs.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Education – mother-tongue education policy; Omniglot
Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Afroasiatic languages; Ethnologue – Eritrea

subtopics.title: Education and public institutions
subtopics.concept: Higher-education colleges (EIT Mai Nefhi, CASS/CBE at Adi Keih, Hamelmalo, Halhale, Orotta, Asmara College of Health Sciences), school system (pre-school at 4–5, elementary 1–5, middle 6–8, secondary 9–12).

textbook_refs.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – ‘The SRSR NUEYS branch …’ (branch offices in the six regions)
Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – newspaper archive (Haddas Ertra, Eritrea Alhaditha, Eritrea Profile); Wikipedia – Media of Eritrea

subtopics.title: Economy, agriculture and development
subtopics.concept: Farming is rain-fed and constrained by soil erosion, land degradation, poor land-use and shortages of inputs, infrastructure and markets; dams (e.g. Kerkebet) and afforestation are remedies.

textbook_refs.reference: IUCN – Pastoralism in Eritrea (country study); UNDP – Eritrea profile (about 80% depend on subsistence crop and livestock farming)
Eritrea Ministry of Energy and Mines / UNDP – household energy in Eritrea
Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com); Danakali Ltd – Colluli Potash Project

topics.title: World geography and international organizations
topics.unit: General Knowledge (no textbook – verified against reliable general sources)
topics.concept: Capitals, borders, seas, rivers, islands and population facts; the UN system and other organizations and where they are based.

subtopics.title: Countries, capitals, seas, rivers and landforms
subtopics.concept: Learn capitals (Warsaw, Khartoum…), coastlines (Mediterranean, Red Sea), river confluences (Blue + White Nile at Khartoum), the Great Rift Valley and population giants (China, India).

textbook_refs.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Standard time; Time zone

subtopics.title: UN agencies and international organizations
subtopics.concept: UN specialised agencies/programmes: FAO (Rome), UNESCO (Paris), UNICEF, UNDP, IAEA… NATO is a military alliance, not a UN body. African Union HQ: Addis Ababa.

textbook_refs.reference: un.org – History of the United Nations

subtopics.title: Arts, culture, explorers and famous people
subtopics.concept: Famous artists (Leonardo da Vinci – Mona Lisa), sports stars (Pelé – Brazil), explorers (Columbus, Vasco da Gama, Magellan – sea voyages; Marco Polo – overland to China), scientists and leaders, oldest instruments (drums/flutes), symbols (Olympic five rings).

textbook_refs.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – The Nurenebi File: a review (16 Dec 2021)

topics.title: Current affairs (time-sensitive)
topics.unit: General Knowledge (no textbook – verified against reliable general sources)
topics.concept: Recent events at the time of the exam: elections, sport, technology releases, diplomacy. Answer as correct at the exam date – facts may have changed since.

subtopics.title: World politics and leaders
subtopics.concept: Know recent elections and changes of leaders, recognitions and blockades in the news in the exam year.

textbook_refs.reference: UN DESA – World Population Prospects 2022; ‘Day of Eight Billion’ (15 Nov 2022)
USGS – M 5.5 Eritrea–Ethiopia region, 26 Dec 2022 (us6000jbsk); Massa et al., landslides of the Dec 26 2022 Northern Red Sea earthquake (Zenodo)
World Health Organization (who.int) fact sheets – Ebola outbreak in Uganda declared over (11 Jan 2023)

subtopics.title: Sport
subtopics.concept: World Cups, Olympic champions, national team nicknames (Bafana Bafana – South Africa; Red Sea Camels – Eritrea).

textbook_refs.reference: Cyclingnews – Biniam Girmay voted African Cyclist of the Year for third time in succession (Dec 2022)
the-sports.org – Daegu Marathon 2022 results; Maeil Shinmun (3 April 2022)

subtopics.title: Technology and media
subtopics.concept: Social media (Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, Skype), smartphones, drones and inventions.

textbook_refs.reference: Tesla Q4 2022 deliveries report; IEA Global EV Outlook 2023

topics.title: Science and health
topics.unit: General Knowledge (no textbook – verified against reliable general sources)
topics.concept: Everyday biology, chemistry and physics: cells and genetics, disease and immunity, properties of matter, elements and compounds, units and measurement.

subtopics.title: Biology, genetics and the human body
subtopics.concept: DNA stores genetic information; 46 chromosomes in a human body cell; mutation = sudden change in genes/chromosomes; phenotype = observable traits; organ systems.

textbook_refs.reference: Patrut et al. (2018) Nature Plants – the demise of the largest and oldest African baobabs

subtopics.title: Health and disease
subtopics.concept: Immunization with vaccines; polio (virus, faecal–oral spread, paralysis, mostly young children); pathology = study of disease.

textbook_refs.reference: World Health Organization (who.int) fact sheets – Vitamin A deficiency
World Health Organization (who.int) fact sheets – Trypanosomiasis, human African (sleeping sickness)
USDA FoodData Central – vitamin C content; WHO – nutrition
Standard science reference (Encyclopaedia Britannica; secondary-school science) – Vitamins

subtopics.title: Chemistry in everyday life
subtopics.concept: Compounds vs elements, noble gases, sodium bicarbonate (baking soda), fermentation (ethanol + CO₂), denatured alcohol (disinfectant), complete vs incomplete combustion (soot).

subtopics.title: Physics and measurement
subtopics.concept: Physical vs chemical properties, temperature scales (Celsius/centigrade, Fahrenheit, Kelvin), the atom (electrons negative), rainbow colours (7).

textbook_refs.reference: Standard science reference (Encyclopaedia Britannica; secondary-school science) – Boiling point and pressure

subtopics.title: Environment and climate change
subtopics.concept: Global warming raises sea level, melts ice, increases drought; pollution is a cause, not a consequence.

textbook_refs.reference: USGS Water Science School – Where is Earth's water?
IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report (2023); NASA Climate – Evidence
US EPA – Overview of greenhouse gases
IPCC AR6 WGIII – emissions by sector
World Health Organization (who.int) fact sheets – Earthquakes fact sheet; CRED/UNDRR – Economic losses, poverty and disasters 1998–2017

topics.title: Agriculture
topics.unit: General Knowledge (no textbook – verified against reliable general sources)
topics.concept: Crops and their uses, soils, plant nutrients and farm management.

subtopics.title: Crops and their uses
subtopics.concept: Cereals (sorghum, barley, wheat, pearl millet), fibre crops (cotton for textiles; sisal/kenaf for ropes and sacks), grapes for wine, common Eritrean vegetables.

textbook_refs.reference: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health – Omega-3 fatty acids; ScienceDirect reviews on plant-derived omega-3

subtopics.title: Farm management and agricultural development
subtopics.concept: Farm management = best use of scarce farm resources for maximum profit and family satisfaction on a continuous basis.

textbook_refs.reference: Eritrean MoE Agriculture/Geography textbooks – land tenure systems (diesa, risti); Land Proclamation 58/1994

topics.title: Economics, business and society
topics.unit: General Knowledge (no textbook – verified against reliable general sources)
topics.concept: Basic economic concepts: investment, interest, employment, economic systems; education systems and social concepts.

subtopics.title: Economic concepts
subtopics.concept: Higher interest raises the cost of borrowing and reduces investment; underemployment = work that does not use a person's full skills/time; capitalism = private ownership and the price system.

textbook_refs.reference: Eritrean MoE Business and Economics – functions of management; Oxford Learner's Dictionary – personnel

subtopics.title: Social concepts
subtopics.concept: Ethnocentrism, archaeology and other social-science terms.

textbook_refs.reference: World Bank / UNDP – characteristics of developed and developing countries

topics.title: Language, idioms and analogies
topics.unit: General Knowledge (no textbook – verified against reliable general sources)
topics.concept: Meanings of sayings and idioms, word formation, figures of speech and analogy patterns.

subtopics.title: Words and figures of speech
subtopics.concept: Prefix/suffix, understatement (making something seem less important than it is), quantitative vs qualitative statements.

textbook_refs.reference: Standard verbal-reasoning practice (dictionary check: throw, theater, that)
Oxford Learner's Dictionary – like (like to do); catch (the game)
Oxford Learner's Dictionary – eradicate, distort, saturate, utilize
Cambridge Dictionary Grammar – adjectives and adverbs

subtopics.title: Analogies and odd-one-out
subtopics.concept: Find the relationship in the first pair (organ → system, landmark → country, animal → home) and apply it to the second.

textbook_refs.reference: Standard science reference (Encyclopaedia Britannica; secondary-school science) – Metals; Petroleum

topics.title: Mathematics and reasoning
topics.unit: General Knowledge (no textbook – verified against reliable general sources)
topics.concept: Percentages, fractions, ratios, primes, clock angles and simple reasoning.

subtopics.title: Percentages, fractions and ratios
subtopics.concept: ‘x% of y% of N’ = x/100 × y/100 × N; 2/5 = 0.4 = 40%; ratio of equal quantities = 1 (1 Nakfa = 100 cents).

subtopics.title: Number facts and reasoning
subtopics.concept: Primes: test divisors up to √n. Clock angle = |30H − 5.5M|.
